judgments.reasoning_cat2: 7.2 cross-refers to "Section 7.7 - Incontestability" while 7.7 is in fact this misstatement clause, so the numbering itself is unsettled across the instrument. Modest relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause contains an unusual carve-out — the two-year bar applies "unless the Surrender Value is insufficient to cover the next Monthly Cost of Insurance" — whose reach (does insufficiency at any moment reopen contestability forever?) is genuinely uncertain. It also runs from the undefined "Issue Date".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That carve-out interlocks with the lapse machinery in 5.10 and 9.4, so a lapse could be argued to revive the insurer's right to contest, which sits awkwardly with 3.4's reinstatement scheme and its own two-year reinstatement bar. A real point of friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-year bar measured from the effective date of each increase, stated simply. The only softness is the implicit reference to the increase's effective date under 6.2.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements the first paragraph of 7.8 and 6.2's increase mechanics without contradiction. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat statement of no participation in earnings and no dividends. As definite as possible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the cover page designation "NONPARTICIPATING". No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The two conditions are stated categorically — no irrevocable beneficiary and no assignment — but taken literally they suspend "every right" of the Owner on any assignment, however limited. That absolute framing is the nameable issue.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 8.3 says only that the Owner's rights "are subject to any assignment", which is narrower than the flat condition here; and 8.4 lets the Owner change a revocable beneficiary. Some tension between 8.1(2) and 8.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is largely destroyed, but the recoverable rule — written notice to the insurer, effective on the date the request was signed, no effect on prior action, policy may be required for endorsement — is conventional. The retroactive-effectiveness feature is the one substantive point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors 8.4's change-of-beneficiary mechanics word for word in effect, so the instrument is internally consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Notification, non-responsibility for validity, and subordination of the Owner's and revocable beneficiary's rights are each stated plainly. No ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies 8.1(2), which conditions the exercise of Owner rights on the policy not having been assigned at all; the two express the assignment consequence differently. Mild tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Default rules are explicit: as shown on the application, else the Owner, and payment to the beneficiary "except as provided in this section". The exception is internal and identified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.4, with Section 1's "AS SPECIFIED ON THE" application, and with 4.1's direction to pay Death Proceeds to the Beneficiary. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The survivorship cascade — beneficiary, then Owner, then Owner's executor or administrator — is complete and determinate. Nothing vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits 8.4's opening default and 4.1's payment rule. Consistent with the whole.
judgments.clause_name: 8.4 - Death of beneficiary before the Insured

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Effectiveness "upon the date your request was signed" combined with "no effect on any payment made before we receive it" creates a retroactive rule with a protective proviso; the interaction can be argued but is expressly addressed. Moderately low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels 8.2's change-of-ownership mechanics and is limited by 8.1's irrevocable-beneficiary condition. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Only a fragment remains — a right to obtain a Policy loan with the Policy as the only security — so the amount, conditions and repayment terms are absent from this text. The residual rule is nonetheless clear as far as it goes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 9.2, 9.3 and 9.4 supply the amount, interest and indebtedness rules, completing the scheme. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The base figure from which the deductions are taken is missing from the legible text, so "the amount [available] less: 1. loan interest to the next anniversary; and 2. Monthly Insurance Charges for the balance of the Policy year" cannot be computed. The formula's starting point is the named gap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The obvious base is the Surrender Value defined in 5.7, and 9.4 uses the same excess-over-indebtedness idea, so the surrounding text points to the answer. Low relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Interest from the date of the loan at "the rate specified in Section" (1), payable annually and on repayment, with capitalisation if unpaid — mechanically clear, though the trailing sentence is clipped. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with 5.2's rule crediting loaned Account Value at the loan rate less two points and with 9.4's definition of indebtedness. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition of indebtedness and the deduction from proceeds are plain; the lapse sentence is a precise sufficiency test. No vague term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its lapse trigger is framed as the excess of Cash Value over indebtedness, while 5.10's trigger is Surrender Value on a Monthly Due Date; these should be arithmetically equal under 5.7 but are separately worded triggers, and 5.10 alone carries the 60-day grace period and notice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The transposed text makes the identification of the payee hard to read, but the rule — beneficiary elects for Death Proceeds, Insured or Owner for other proceeds, subject to Section 8 — is recoverable. Moderate-low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The reference to Section 8 correctly picks up ownership, assignment and beneficiary constraints; no operative conflict appears. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Single lump payment at claim settlement to the payee; nothing to interpret. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.1 and 4.3's interest-to-settlement rule. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is garbled around "the present value, which is equal to the Policy Proceeds using the rate then declared by us" and it is unclear whether the 4% floor governs the crediting rate or the payment computation. That is a genuine wording knot in a payment formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Fixed Period table that follows and 10.2's basis-of-options rule supply concrete guaranteed amounts, largely resolving it. Low relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The illustrative figure "$6,384" is plainly a mistranscription of a per-$1,000 monthly amount (compare $6.77 and the table's $6.38), and the guarantee period is rendered "0 year"; the numbers as printed do not cohere. Those are nameable mechanical errors in a benefit illustration.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Payments for Life table below gives male age 65 at 6.72/6.62/6.38/5.40/5.24, which does not exactly match the 6.77 quoted here — a small numerical divergence between text and table.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The joint-life option survives only in fragments, with the opening words lost, but its structure (income during two lives, optional guaranteed period, rates furnished on request) is discernible. Rates left to be "furnished upon request" are less definite than the other options.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Unlike Options 2, 3 and 5, no guaranteed rate or table is provided for Option 4, but 10.2 supplies a general basis, so the omission is filled generally. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is clipped so that the withdrawal-limitation proviso ends mid-word ("unless the B B"), leaving the restriction on withdrawals unstated. The 4% minimum interest and annual payment default are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The missing proviso evidently refers to a beneficiary designation limiting withdrawals, a concept 8.4 supports; 10.2's basis-of-options rule also applies. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Determining amounts using "our rates in effect at the time of settlement" is definite in mechanism, though it leaves the rate to the insurer subject to the guarantees in the individual options. The present-value equivalence sentence is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with Options 2, 3 and 5, each of which sets a guaranteed floor (4%, tabled amounts), so a settlement-time rate could be argued to override those floors — a point of tension the clause does not expressly resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single informational sentence with no obligation or standard. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It merely supplements the monthly table in Option 2. Consistent.
judgments.clause_name: Annual, semi-annual or quarterly payment amounts

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of elective guarantee periods is corrupted ("not less than % 10, Ss, -or 20 yegrs"), so the available options are not fully legible, though the table headings (5, 10, 15, 20 years certain) supply them. Minor mechanical defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The accompanying table's column headings resolve the garbled list, and Option 3 describes the same choice. Consistent.
